Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciated you and Sara walking us through the integration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Integration scope: text generation + embeddings + reranker for search relevance.
- SDK setup: prefer server-side SDK for backend calls; client-side only for limited UX tokens.
- Auth options discussed: API keys (simple), service accounts (recommended for server-to-server), OAuth2 client-credentials + JWT assertions for short-lived tokens.
- Key management: rotate programmatically (recommended 30-90 day cadence), store keys in customer KMS/HSM, Redwood supports KMS integrations for envelope encryption.
- Routing & structured output: route sensitive requests to dedicated pools; tool-calling/structured outputs require explicit scopes.

Recommendations (high level):
1) Use a service account per application + short-lived JWT tokens issued by your authn layer for server-to-server calls.
2) Keep embeddings/semantic-ranking keys separate from generation keys (different scopes/quotas) - easier to revoke and audit.
3) Configure automatic key rotation in your KMS; Redwood can accept rotated public keys or short-lived tokens (we support JWKS & introspection endpoints).
4) Start with sandboxed routing (test pool) and a per-route policy for embeddings vs. generation.

Attachments: redwood-authn-overview.pdf (high-level flows), redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (examples).

Next steps / action items:
- You: Confirm which internal teams will attend a technical follow-up (security + backend eng).
- Us: We'll produce a short architecture note with sample JWT claims, example service-account setup, and a rotation playbook.
- Schedule: propose 30-45 minute technical sync next week.

Does that look right? If so, I'll loop in our engineering lead and drop a draft architecture note into a shared Drive.

Thanks Marissa — I'll draft the architecture note and rotation playbook. High-level answers now so you can share with Alex if helpful: 

- Introspection: We support both JWKS (public key discovery) for verifying JWTs and an OAuth2 token-introspection endpoint for short-lived tokens. We also emit token-related events to audit logs (token_id, subject, exp, issued_at, client_id).

- Rotation & rollback (short):
  1) Create new key in KMS and deploy to staging.
  2) Add new key to JWKS and keep old key active (dual-write) for the overlap window.
  3) Validate in staging and run smoke tests calling Redwood sandbox.
  4) Update production services to request tokens signed by the new key.
  5) Monitor error rates and audit logs for token validation failures.
  6) If failures spike, revert clients to previous key and remove new key from production JWKS.

- Embeddings vs generation keys: We recommend per-microservice service accounts with scoped roles (embedding:read, embedding:write, generation:call). Put an API gateway in front and enforce quotas per key.

I'll put the detailed playbook and sample JWT claim set (iss/sub/aud/exp/nbf/iat/jti + example scopes) into a Drive doc and drop the link here tomorrow: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AuthnDraft

Proposed next step: schedule 30-45m tech sync Wed 2027-08-18 09:30 PDT — I can join with a short demo of the token exchange and rotation flow.
